horizon.status: Newest measurement: Claude Mythos Preview (early checkpoint, released Apr 2026), about 17 h at 50% success (95% CI 8.5–55 h) and about 3 h at 80% (1.6–6.6 h). The 50% figure is above the 16 h where METR says its task suite stops being reliable. No model released since has a published time horizon (see other readings), so today's values are projections at METR's post-2023 doubling time of 3.4–5.2 months; the 80% series has doubled at the same pace (about every 4.4 months since 2023 on METR's data).

other_readings.subject: Public frontier, Feb–Mar 2026
other_readings.note: METR puts the unreleased internal frontier at 16–20 h (50%) and 3–4 h (80%), about two months ahead.

other_readings.subject: GPT-5.6 Sol
other_readings.note: METR says this is not a robust measurement: its rate of cheating on tests was higher than any public model METR had evaluated. Dropping the cheating attempts gives 71 h.

other_readings.subject: Claude Opus 5.5
other_readings.note: No time horizon reported. METR used five long AI-research tasks instead and calls it an incremental step above Claude Fable 5.1.

other_readings.subject: Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.7
other_readings.note: A different yardstick: rebuild a real program from its behaviour. Opus 4.6 rebuilt a 16,000-line toolkit that would take a human engineer an estimated 2–17 weeks; Opus 4.7 did it in 14 hours. Scored as tests passed, not a time horizon.

headline: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon (59) leads the Artificial Analysis index, one point ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (58) and two ahead of GPT-6 Astra (57); for value, GPT-6.1 Sol scores 55 at about $1.27 per task and GPT-6.1 Terra 51 at about $0.96.

The best open models (GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, both 32) trail the closed frontier (59) by 27 points, roughly 4 months behind on Epoch’s lag estimate; Mistral Large 4 went open yesterday at 26, and if Moonshot publishes Kimi K3.1 Pro's weights (46) by 4 November as promised, the gap shrinks to 13 points.
An open model matching Gemini 4 Carbon (59) is expected around Feb 2027 (range Jan 2027 to Apr 2027); a version that runs on a desktop under AUD 50k about 2 months later.

changelog.why: Split from the brain-equivalence dashboard into a daily-updated public data file.

changelog.what: Added Muse Spark Open (Meta, open, AA 39) and Mistral Large 4 Preview (closed for now, AA 38); AUD/USD 1.405 → 1.440.
changelog.why: Both are now scored on AA index v4.3.2 (artificialanalysis.ai model pages); neither moves a frontier. FX moved more than 1% (tradingeconomics, 17 Oct).

changelog.what: Task-length series rebuilt on METR Time Horizon 1.1, now ending at Claude Mythos Preview (~17 h) instead of Claude Opus 4.6; points carry 95% CIs. Horizon doubling 4–7 → 3.4–5.2 months. Open-model lag 4/5/7 → 3/4/6 months. Headline 3 now targets the current best closed model.
changelog.why: METR's results file lists Mythos Preview (added 8 May 2026) and gives v1.1 values for older models that differed from ours; its post-2023 doubling time is 128.7 days (CI 104–158). Epoch's 29 May 2026 Data Insight puts the open-model lag at 4 months since Jan 2026, about 6 under strict dominance (epoch.ai/data-insights/open-closed-eci-gap).

changelog.what: Task length now shows 80% success alongside 50%, uses METR's full state-of-the-art series (18 models, 2019–2026) with 95% CIs, and lists other published readings (METR Frontier Risk Report, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, MirrorCode).
changelog.why: 80% values are in METR's Time Horizon 1.1 results file; a fit of its 80% frontier points gives a doubling of 133 days since 2023, in line with the 50% series (129 days), so the same 3.4–5.2 month band applies. No model released after April 2026 has a published time horizon (checked METR's blog and Epoch on 2026-10-18).

changelog.what: Added DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (open, MIT, AA 45) and MiniMax M3.1 Flash (closed for now, AA 42); the September DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is marked superseded.
changelog.why: Both are now scored on AA index v4.3.2 (artificialanalysis.ai model pages); DeepSeek's pricing page says the 1017 checkpoint now serves deepseek-flash at unchanged prices. Neither moves a frontier: 45 is below MiMo-V2.6-Pro's 46, and DeepSeek's 552B weights do not fit a 256GB desktop at 4-bit.

changelog.what: Added Kimi K3.1 Pro (Moonshot, closed for now, AA 55). MiniMax M3.1 Flash reclassified as open (428B / 23B active, MiniMax Community Licence) and its AA index updated 42 → 43.
changelog.why: Kimi K3.1 Pro is scored on AA index v4.3.2 (artificialanalysis.ai/models/kimi-k3-1-pro, $2.11 per task); AA says its weights are not yet published, so it does not count as open. MiniMax's weights went up on Hugging Face on 23 Oct (huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash), and AA's model page now shows 43. No frontier moves: 55 is below 58, 43 is below the open best of 46, and the 252 GB checkpoint has no verified 256GB-desktop run.

changelog.what: Added GPT-6.1 Terra (OpenAI, closed, AA 48, $1/$5 per million tokens). AA cost per task updated: Gemini 4 Argon $1.99 → $1.62, Muse Wonder $4.52 → $8.63 (cache read $0.20). AUD/USD 1.440 → 1.425.
changelog.why: Terra is scored on AA index v4.3.2 (artificialanalysis.ai/models/gpt-6-1-terra, $0.40 per task); prices from AA and OpenAI's announcement (community.openai.com), cached input $0.05. No frontier moves: 48 is below 58. The two cost figures are what AA's model pages now show. FX moved more than 1% (tradingeconomics, 26 Oct: 0.7017 USD per AUD).

changelog.what: AA cost per task updated: Muse Wonder $8.63 → $3.27, Grok 4.7 (high) $2.73 → $2.36, Mistral Large 4 Preview now $1.61 (was unknown). Grok 4.7 output price added: $6 per million tokens.
changelog.why: These are the figures AA's leaderboard and model pages now show (artificialanalysis.ai/models/muse-wonder, /grok-4-7, /mistral-large-4). No scores or frontiers moved. Mistral Large 4 weights missed the reported 27 Oct date (Hugging Face ETA 31 Oct); Kimi K3.1 Pro weights are due by 4 Nov, so both stay closed for now.

changelog.what: Artificial Analysis index v4.3.2 → v5.0: every aa_index, cost per task and history value re-baselined to AA's v5 figures. Added Gemini 4 Carbon (Google, closed, AA 59, new #1; $2/$10 intro). Closed frontier is now Fable 5.1 49 → GPT-6 Astra 57 → Opus 5.5 58 → Gemini 4 Carbon 59; open frontier DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 23 → GLM-5.3 32; local MiMo-V2.6-Flash 27. Headline 3 now targets Gemini 4 Carbon.
changelog.why: AA published Intelligence Index v5 on 27 Oct (artificialanalysis.ai/articles/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index-v5): new and harder benchmarks, more private test sets, so v4.3.2 and v5 scores are not comparable. Scores and costs are from each AA model page on 29 Oct. AA gives no v5 score for Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3-Flash or the September DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, so their aa_index is now null and the Fable 5, Opus 5 and Kimi K3 history points were removed (each side still has at least 2 points); MiMo-V2.6-Pro (30 on v5) no longer sets the open frontier. GPT-6 Astra joins the closed envelope because on v5 it beats Fable 5.1 at its release. The local series moves from GLM-5.3-Flash (unscored) to MiMo-V2.6-Flash. Forecast parameters are unchanged: AA has not published a v5 growth trend, so 1.5 points a month is still on the v4 scale.

changelog.what: Added Mistral Large 4 (Mistral, open, AA 26, $0.70/$2.10 per million tokens, $2.06 per task); Mistral Large 4 Preview marked superseded.
changelog.why: Weights went up on Hugging Face on 29 Oct under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B); AA's model page now lists it as open weights, released 29 Oct, with the score, cost per task, prices and a 90% cache discount ($0.07 cached input). No frontier moves: 26 is below the open best of 32, and the smallest checkpoint (610 GB NVFP4, orcarouter.ai) does not fit a 512GB desktop.
